methodological_rigor.justification: IDeate-Lung01 is a preregistered (NCT05280470), multicenter, global, two-part, open-label phase II trial with a clear dose-optimization (8 vs 12 mg/kg) randomization stratified by prior anti-PD-(L)1 and CTFI-based strata, followed by an extension at the selected 12 mg/kg dose. Primary endpoint is confirmed ORR by blinded independent central review per RECIST 1.1, with preplanned secondary endpoints, subgroup analyses, and an independent ILD adjudication committee. The sample size is justified (n~100 provides 99% probability CI lower bound exceeds 20% benchmark). Limitations are the absence of a concurrent control arm (acknowledged), open-label design, and that 95% CIs are not multiplicity-adjusted — but these are appropriate to a phase II dose-optimization trial.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Previously treated ES-SCLC is a high-unmet-need setting where approved options (topotecan, lurbinectedin, amrubicin) offer ORR 7-31% and median OS 6-9 months. The trial demonstrates ORR 48.2%, DOR 5.3 months, PFS 4.9 months, and OS 10.3 months with I-DXd 12 mg/kg, including intracranial activity (CNS ORR 46.2%) and 56.3% ORR in second-line. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation was granted and a phase III (IDeate-Lung02) is ongoing, establishing direct clinical relevance. Oxford LoE 2b as a single-arm phase II (low-quality RCT equivalent for LoE purposes).

reporting_quality.justification: The paper reports a CONSORT diagram, prespecified endpoints, stratified randomization details (permuted blocks of 4 via IRT), and comprehensive safety with AESI categories, ILD adjudication, and detailed time-to-event reporting. Inclusion/exclusion, dose modifications, and data cutoff (March 3, 2025) are clearly stated. While CONSORT checklist adherence is not explicitly cited, most CONSORT items are addressed. Data and supplemental tables are provided; no statement about patient-level data sharing is visible, but the trial is a registered sponsor-funded industry trial with typical data-on-request framework.

novelty_literature.justification: Ifinatamab deruxtecan is a first-in-class B7-H3-directed ADC, and this is the primary phase II analysis establishing its efficacy and safety in previously treated ES-SCLC. Comparisons with tarlatamab, topotecan, amrubicin, and lurbinectedin position I-DXd as a potentially best-in-class chemotherapy-free option with notable CNS activity. Novelty is strong given the target (B7-H3) and the mechanism, though not field-defining until phase III confirmation.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear sections, detailed subgroup analyses, and appropriate framing of benefit-risk (including ILD surveillance). Tables 1-5 and Figure 2 panels A-E communicate efficacy, safety, and subgroup results effectively. Discussion thoughtfully compares with tarlatamab (DeLLphi-301/304) and historical second-line options while acknowledging cross-trial caveats. Some dense sections on CTFI subgroups could be streamlined.

key_strengths: Global multicenter phase II at 57 sites with preregistered primary endpoint (NCT05280470)
Strong efficacy in high-unmet-need ES-SCLC: ORR 48.2%, median OS 10.3 months, PFS 4.9 months with I-DXd 12 mg/kg
Notable CNS activity (CNS ORR 46.2%, CR 30.8%) in patients with baseline brain metastases
First-in-class B7-H3 ADC with FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation; phase III IDeate-Lung02 underway
Rigorous independent central review, ILD adjudication committee, and BICR-investigator concordance
key_concerns: Single-arm noncomparative phase II without a standard-of-care control arm
ILD/pneumonitis in 12.4% including 2 grade 5 treatment-related deaths requires careful surveillance
Underrepresentation of Black patients and lower ORR in North America (32.3%) vs Asia (51.5%) and Europe (55.0%)
Open-label design introduces potential assessment bias despite BICR
DOR of 5.3 months is shorter than tarlatamab's reported 6.9-9.7 months, with OS maturity pending for part 2
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed phase II of a first-in-class B7-H3 ADC showing best-in-class activity in previously treated ES-SCLC with FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation; content merits tier-1 placement with minor revisions pending phase III confirmation.
